papers.title: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals: accessing generic orbits
papers.abstract: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRI) are a significant gravitational wave source and a target for the upcoming LISA mission. Computations of the fluxes of conserved quantities, such as energy and angular momentum, are a critical part of modeling EMRI waveforms and can be performed using a frequency domain formalism to solve the Teukolsky equation. This requires computations of large numbers of mode amplitudes, many of which are negligible. However, it is unknown ex ante which can be safely skipped. We present a machine learning approach to estimate the dominant radial mode number as a function of the remaining mode numbers and apply it to reduce the number of unnecessary computations in EMRI flux calculation.

ai_review.summary: This proof-of-concept study uses a neural network to predict which radial harmonic dominates a generic-orbit EMRI flux calculation. Frequency-domain Teukolsky computations supply labels for combinations of orbital parameters and mode indices. A nonlinear network substantially outperforms a model linear in the mode numbers: rounded predictions match 88.6% of test labels exactly and 98.5% within one harmonic. The intended benefit is to locate promising modes before spending time on negligible contributions. However, the reported tests split mode samples from the same orbits across training and evaluation, and all backgrounds have spin 0.9. The paper therefore establishes an encouraging mode-selection estimator, rather than a validated general-purpose flux accelerator or a demonstrated waveform-accuracy guarantee.
ai_review.relevance_reason: Directly addresses EMRI modeling, Teukolsky fluxes and generic Kerr orbits, with potential computational benefits for perturbative waveform generation.
ai_review.quality_reason: A baseline comparison, explicit training setup and quantitative test errors support the restricted proof of concept. Shared orbits across data splits and a single spin weaken evidence of generalization; end-to-end speed and flux-error validation remain necessary.
ai_review.limitations: Selective text reading: abstract/introduction, Sec. 2 dataset/truncation excerpts, Sec. 4 network results and Sec. 5 conclusions. No unseen-orbit validation or broad spin coverage; dominant-mode accuracy does not establish total-flux accuracy. No visual figure inspection, training execution or independent derivation verification.

papers.title: EMRI Dephasing from a Torsion-Inspired Near-Zone Kerr Deformation: Motivated by Spin-Polarized Dark Matter
papers.abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are sensitive probes of weak conservative perturbations in the strong-field region of massive black holes. We study a phenomenological EMRI model motivated by Einstein--Cartan gravity in which a spin-polarized dark-matter spike is described by a Weyssenhoff fluid. After torsion is eliminated algebraically, the local spin contribution contains a repulsive exterior source $U_{tt}^{\rm spin}\propto-σ_0^2/r^3$. Solving the corresponding static linearized field equation, however, does not produce a global $1/r^3$ metric perturbation; the response contains a mass renormalization, a logarithmic $r^{-1}$ tail, and an $M/r^2$ term. We therefore introduce $g_{μν}^{\rm eff}=g_{μν}^{\rm Kerr}+αh_{μν}^{\rm eff}$ only as a local near-zone matching ansatz, not as a complete rotating Einstein--Cartan black-hole solution. Within this torsion-inspired deformation we compute circular equatorial inspirals and analytic-kludge waveforms. The fiducial model can produce large phase shifts in an idealized adiabatic calculation, but the forecast is optimistic and does not include a full LISA/Taiji response, Teukolsky/self-force fluxes, eccentricity, inclination, or high-dimensional parameter degeneracies. The results should be read as constraints on an effective near-zone operator rather than as a prediction of minimally coupled Einstein--Cartan dark matter.

ai_review.summary: This paper separates conditional EMRI phase diagnostics from a proposed spin-matter interpretation. For a prescribed near-zone Kerr deformation, circular-equatorial orbital calculations and a frozen numerical Kerr flux give about −436 radians of conservative dephasing for the chosen benchmark. Comparing another metric with the same leading asymptotic correction produces a much smaller shift, demonstrating dependence on the full metric prescription. Separate spherical Einstein–Cartan appendices report spin-ensemble closure, finite-cloud evolution and coupled metric–matter radiation calculations; these do not derive the rotating ansatz. The useful contribution is an explicit separation of conservative geometry, dissipative assumptions and microphysics. Large phase shifts are not detector forecasts, and a physical source-to-metric map, consistent rotating fluxes and parameter inference are still needed.
ai_review.relevance_reason: Directly concerns EMRI dephasing, environmental effects, modified Kerr geometry and coupled matter–metric perturbations.
ai_review.quality_reason: The inspected text supplies quantitative vacuum checks, alternative flux/metric comparisons and refinement diagnostics in a separate spherical calculation. These support conditional results, but do not validate the rotating deformation as a sourced model or its observational interpretation.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading: abstract/introduction, Sec. VI interpretation, Sec. VII conclusions, Appendix A checks and portions of Appendix D. The long spin-transport derivations and complete radiation system were not verified. Circular-equatorial rotating results use an assumed flux; spherical radiation results concern a different model. No visual figure inspection or code execution.

papers.title: The Geometric Imprint of a Tilted Accretion Disk in Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: Gravitational wave astronomy has opened a new window onto black holes and the dynamics of strong-field gravity, while accretion flows offer a complementary and natural laboratory for probing strong-field physics. In this work, we show that the gravitational wave emission from an initially tilted accretion disk carries a distinct imprint of its orientation. We perform three dimensional general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations and evaluate the gravitational waves through Teukolsky equation. For an aligned disk, the emission is concentrated in low-$|m|$ modes, where $m$ is the azimuthal quantum number. For the initially tilted disk, higher-$|m|$ modes make a larger relative contribution. As the tilted flow subsequently aligns with the black hole spin, the contribution of $|m|\ge2$ modes decreases, showing strong correlation with the tilt angle. This indicates that the gravitational waves generated by the black hole environment carries geometric information about the surrounding matter. Our results establish a route towards using multimode gravitational radiation to probe the geometry and dynamical evolution of accretion flows in the strong-field region.

ai_review.summary: The study asks whether gravitational radiation from an accretion flow records the disk’s tilt relative to a spinning black hole. Two matched three-dimensional GRMHD simulations, initially aligned or tilted by 75 degrees, supply stress–energy sources for time-domain Teukolsky calculations on a fixed Kerr background. The tilted flow contributes more power to higher azimuthal modes; as it aligns, the high-mode fraction declines alongside the measured tilt. Mode-cutoff checks and MRI resolution diagnostics support the numerical example, while a rotated-axis model provides a geometric interpretation. This connects disk dynamics to a potentially useful multimode gravitational-wave signature. Generality and observability remain open: only two initial orientations and one spin are studied, and the illustrative strain rescaling is not a detector-inference analysis.
ai_review.relevance_reason: Combines GRMHD, Teukolsky radiation, environmental geometry and gravitational waves, directly matching several central topics.
ai_review.quality_reason: Matched simulations, mode-cutoff comparisons and MRI diagnostics substantiate the reported correlation. A narrow simulation set and idealized strain rescaling limit claims of universal tilt recovery or detectability.

Fixed background, single spin and two initial tilts; disk self-gravity and detector parameter recovery are not assessed here. Mode-cutoff agreement is not a full numerical-resolution study. No visual figure inspection, simulation execution or derivation verification.

papers.title: Complete quasinormal modes of Type-D black holes. III. Reissner-Nordström spectra from zero to extremal charge
papers.abstract: Earlier calculations left open how gravitational quasinormal modes (QNMs) of charged black holes recover the Schwarzschild spectrum and how the modes near algebraically special frequencies relate to the exact special solutions. We extend our Kerr analysis to Reissner-Nordström black holes by analytically continuing the ingoing horizon solution and locating the zeros of the incoming amplitude at infinity. For each of $\ell=2$ and $3$, we trace the first 42 overtone families from the Schwarzschild limit to extremality. The charge trajectories distinguish crossings of the negative imaginary axis from turns near it and separate the unconventional Schwarzschild modes from neighboring branches. At zero charge the polar algebraically special mode is a QNM. At extremal charge the exact axial special modes are total-transmission modes. Of the 84 families, 75 approach distinct extremal frequencies with finite damping, and nine approach zero frequency with vanishing excitation. At exact extremality we also compute, for the first time, gravitational QNMs on the unconventional Riemann sheet reached across the negative imaginary axis. At intermediate charge, the clearest resonant enhancement of both excitation factors occurs for the $\ell=3$ overtone pairs $(22,23)$ and $(23,24)$.

ai_review.summary: This spectral survey follows charged-black-hole gravitational quasinormal modes through crossings of the negative imaginary frequency axis. Analytic continuation of the ingoing horizon solution identifies zeros of the incoming amplitude at infinity, with a separate construction at exact extremality. For angular orders two and three, the authors trace 42 overtone families each: 75 retain finite damping at extremality, while nine approach zero frequency with vanishing excitation. The analysis also distinguishes algebraically special quasinormal and total-transmission solutions, and identifies strong excitation-factor resonances between selected overtones. Detailed residual and parameter-refinement checks support this bounded survey. It supplies useful mode identities and continuation seeds, but neither proves completeness for all angular orders and overtones nor establishes source-dependent ringdown amplitudes.

The inspected validation concerns numerical consistency rather than independent reproduction.

papers.title: Modeling the gravitational wave spectrum from slowly-evolving sources in the early Universe: constant-in-time and coherent-decay models
papers.abstract: We study the production of gravitational wave (GW) backgrounds from slowly-evolving sources in the early Universe, following the Constant-in-Time (CiT) model, presented and validated against simulations of decaying turbulence in arXiv:2201.05630. We extend the CiT model to account for the source decay using a coherent description for the unequal-time correlator (UETC) of the source. We present a generic framework that allows us to study different types of sources. As examples, we discuss the applicability of this framework to the production of GWs from decaying MHD turbulence, sound waves, and bubble collisions in first-order phase transitions. We show that the validity of the CiT and the coherent-decay models presented in this work relies on long decorrelation times of the source. However, as the decorrelation timescale of the UETC becomes short, a resonant term grows on top of the GW spectrum predicted by the CiT model, as found, for example, in earlier analytical studies of GW production from turbulence and sound waves. This model is compatible with previous numerical results and explains why sound waves in a radiation-dominated fluid are more efficient than subrelativistic MHD turbulence in producing GWs, which is no longer the case for relativistic turbulence. The CiT model predicts a generic spectrum that scales as $k^3$ in the IR regime, develops a linear $k$ at intermediate frequencies, and decays as $k^{1-b_Π}$ at frequencies above the inverse correlation length scale of the source, where $b_Π$ is uniquely determined by the type of source and the UV slope of its spectrum. Since the $k^3$ and $k$ scalings always appear for slowly-evolving sources and they are commonly found in studies of GW production, we motivate checking the potential applicability of the CiT to other sources of GWs.

ai_review.summary: The abstract describes a framework for gravitational-wave backgrounds generated by slowly evolving early-Universe sources. Starting from a constant-in-time source model, the authors incorporate decay through a coherent unequal-time correlator and discuss applications to MHD turbulence, sound waves and bubble collisions. They report that long source-decorrelation times support the constant-in-time or coherent-decay description, whereas short decorrelation can add a resonant contribution. The proposed spectrum rises cubically in the infrared, has an intermediate linear regime and acquires a source-dependent ultraviolet slope. The framework aims to explain differing radiation efficiencies of sound waves and turbulence and unify several source classes. These are abstract-level claims here: the derivations, numerical comparisons and range of applicability were unavailable within the review’s text-size limit.

papers.title: Shaping black hole resonances I: Black hole ringdown as a spectral filtering process
papers.abstract: The ringdown of a perturbed black hole (BH) can be described as a superposition of quasinormal modes (QNMs), whose frequencies are determined by the spacetime geometry while their amplitudes depend also on the perturbing source. However, the physical mechanism governing mode excitation remains unclear and is typically treated on a case by case basis. In this work, we show that QNM excitation is governed by a simple spectral rule: each mode is excited according to the Fourier content of the perturbation evaluated at its characteristic frequency. This result follows from the factorization of the excitation coefficients and establishes a direct, quantitative connection between the spectral properties of the perturbation and the resulting ringdown amplitudes. To make this mechanism explicit and controllable, we construct localized perturbations with independently tunable spectral bandwidth and carrier frequency. We demonstrate analytically and numerically that BHs act as resonant spectral filters. We show analytically that the excitation amplitude of each mode equals the weighted spatial Fourier transform of the initial data evaluated at wavenumber $k\simω_n$ so that the filter selectively excites modes whose frequencies lie within the spectral support of the perturbation while suppressing others. Consequently, the excitation is maximized when the dominant perturbation frequency lies close to the real part of the QNM frequency, and we validate this at the percent level with fits to time-domain numerical evolutions. To robustly perform these fits, we have developed a new fitting algorithm, $\mathtt{QNMToolkit}$, which performs ringdown fits over large ensembles of sliding time-domain windows and quantifies the resulting fitting variance.

ai_review.summary: This paper interprets black-hole ringdown excitation as spectral filtering of the perturbation. Factoring each excitation coefficient into a background response and a source overlap shows that the relevant spectrum is weighted by the quasinormal-mode wavefunction; it reduces to an ordinary Fourier transform for distant initial data. Tunable Gaussian pulses vary bandwidth and carrier frequency, allowing selective mode excitation. Regge–Wheeler evolutions, full radial-wavefunction calculations and asymptotic predictions agree closely in the tested regime, while sliding-window fits expose tail contamination and fitting ambiguity. The contribution is a quantitative, controllable interpretation of source-dependent ringdown amplitudes. Applications to rotating holes and nonlinear merger waveforms remain extensions, and window-to-window spread should not be read as a calibrated statistical posterior.

ai_review.quality_reason: Analytic factorization, two radial descriptions and direct time-domain comparisons provide complementary support for the tested pulse families. The paper explicitly identifies tail-driven fit floors and finite-source-location limitations.

Demonstrations concern linear Regge–Wheeler evolutions and controlled initial pulses, not observed mergers or Kerr waveform inference. Fit-window dispersion is an empirical systematic diagnostic. papers.title: Fuzzy Dark Matter as a diffractive barrier: Wave-optics Signatures of Ultralight Fields on Lensed Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves (GWs) propagate through the universe from sources at high redshift, experiencing the gravitational fields of the intervening matter distribution. Halos composed of ultralight dark matter (ULDM) contain strong density fluctuations, reflecting the interference pattern in the field distribution of the ultralight bosons. In the wave-optics regime, ULDM fluctuations act as a diffractive grating, imprinting frequency-dependent modulations of GWs, in addition to magnification and other gravitational lensing effects. Since lensing depends on the projected surface density, we derive its approximate probability distribution and show how it departs from a Gaussian distribution depending on the halo profile and coherence length. We then quantify how the GW diffraction signatures produced by the granules depend on macroimage magnification and parity. The ULDM interference network imprints stochastic diffraction fluctuations at the $O(1)\%$ level on GWs moderately lensed by the host when the Fresnel scale is comparable to the granule coherence length $r_F(f)\sim\ell_c$. These fluctuations can be enhanced to $\gtrsim10\%$ when the host macroimage forms near the critical curve or for Type II macroimages. For massive black hole binaries observed by LISA, the diffraction signature can be detectable around the ULDM particle mass $m_φ\sim10^{-21}$ eV, providing either a smoking-gun signature of ULDM or new constraints on $m_φ$.

ai_review.summary: Ultralight-dark-matter interference granules can act as a random diffractive screen for strongly lensed gravitational waves. The authors construct projected density realizations from a Gaussian field covariance and compute their full wave-optics response around minimum and saddle macroimages. Modulations become strongest when the Fresnel scale approaches the granule coherence length, reaching percent levels in benchmark halos and larger values near critical curves. LISA massive-black-hole-binary examples suggest distinguishability near boson masses of 10⁻²¹ eV. A Fourier implementation is checked against contour integration for minimum images. The contribution is a statistical granular-lensing model beyond leading Born order. However, fixed intrinsic source parameters make the detectability estimates optimistic; realistic halo correlations, smooth-lens degeneracies and full inference are still required.

The paper clearly limits its mismatch-based detectability criterion and near-critical host approximation.

papers.title: Stochastic gravitational waves from narrow-band cosmological magnetic fields
papers.abstract: We calculate the spectrum of gravitational waves generated by a cosmological magnetic field with a narrow-band power spectrum. For a magnetic spectrum narrowly peaked at a comoving wavenumber $k_c$, we find that the gravitational wave signal has a maximum at $2k_c$ and, as expected from momentum conservation, has a sharp cutoff at that scale. We apply this analysis to an ultralight dark matter model of magnetogenesis operating around recombination, in which an axion-photon coupling generates a helical magnetic field by parametric resonance. We determine the conditions for the resulting gravitational waves to enter the frequency range of pulsar timing experiments. Although the required frequency can be reached for sufficiently large coupling, the corresponding amplitude is below the experimental sensitivity for physically allowed energy densities of the magnetic field. We generalize this conclusion to models of magnetogenesis operating at other epochs, estimating as $T \simeq 160$ MeV the temperature of a magnetogenesis process assumed to be the source of the stochastic gravitational wave background suggested by pulsar timing arrays. We place the lower bound $T \gtrsim 1$-10 MeV on such viable models.

ai_review.summary: The authors calculate gravitational-wave production from a cosmological magnetic field concentrated in a narrow band of wavenumbers. Approximating that band by a delta function makes the anisotropic-stress convolution analytic, producing a spectrum with a peak and sharp cutoff at twice the magnetic wavenumber. Applied to an ultralight-axion magnetogenesis scenario near recombination, the attainable signal is too weak to explain pulsar-timing backgrounds at allowed magnetic energy densities. Scaling the calculation to earlier generation epochs gives a conditional estimate near 160 MeV and a rough lower temperature range of 1–10 MeV for viable explanations. This provides a useful analytic mapping from magnetic structure to gravitational radiation, but broader spectra, evolving turbulence and data-level likelihood comparisons can change its quantitative interpretation.

papers.title: Convergence of the quasinormal-mode expansion of the Kerr Green function
papers.abstract: Black-hole ringdown is usually modeled as a linear superposition of quasinormal modes, and fits to gravitational-wave observations increasingly include high overtones. However, the overtone sum does not necessarily converge: overtones are more strongly damped and thus decay faster in time, but their amplitudes in the Green function (the signal at an observer produced by an impulse at a source point) grow, so the mode description may break down before a finite time. We show that for a rotating (Kerr) black hole this time has a clear geometric meaning. For highly damped modes, the amplitudes grow exponentially with the optical distance from the source and the observer to a characteristic "bounce" radius close to the black hole, defined as the location where the mode amplitude is smallest. For one family of modes, the amplitudes are also suppressed the farther the source and observer sit from the equatorial plane. Rotation therefore makes the onset of convergence depend on direction as well as distance, extending the geometric picture from bounce radii to bounce surfaces. Combining these effects gives a sufficient condition for absolute convergence. For spin $a/M = 0.7$, we map how this time varies with source and observer position, and amplitudes computed numerically reproduce the predicted spatial dependence to better than one percent. These results set geometric limits on when the quasinormal-mode sums converge.

ai_review.summary: This work derives a geometric sufficient condition for convergence of Kerr quasinormal-mode overtone sums at fixed angular indices. High-damping asymptotics relate the growth of Green-function pole amplitudes to optical distances from source and observer to characteristic bounce radii. Different angular behavior of prolate and oblate mode families introduces directional dependence and bounce surfaces. Numerical amplitudes at spin 0.7 reproduce the predicted spatial growth rates to better than one percent on the tested grid. The contribution is a concrete boundary for absolute convergence of these pole sums, relevant to interpreting early ringdown fits. It is not a complete representation of the causal response: nonpole contributions remain necessary, and an extended physical source requires integration over its emitting history and position.

ai_review.quality_reason: The asymptotic growth criterion, angular/radial decomposition, Schwarzschild limit and direct checks of complete pole amplitudes provide complementary support. The inspected numerical comparison is bounded in spin and sampled positions; full-source implications remain to be developed.

papers.title: Beyond the point lens: radial structure and the horizon in wave-optics gravitational lensing
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave lensing in the wave-optics regime is sensitive to the structure of the lens beyond its total mass: to its exterior radial profile and, as we show, to the boundary condition at its centre. We develop an analytic framework to compute these effects for a scalar wave, as corrections to the wave lensed by a Newtonian point mass. The corrections are organized in inverse powers of the distance from the lens and computed with dressed radial kernels, which include the Newtonian interaction to all orders and resum the long-range phase that invalidates the Born expansion around the free wave. Retaining wavefront curvature, we find that the scattered wave is not the whole response: an inverse-square deformation changes the direct wave by an equal amount, even when the scattered wave is faint. Steeper terms of the exterior potential lead to short-distance divergences, which signal that the exterior geometry alone does not determine the lensed wave: the missing information is a set of local terms fixed by the inner boundary condition. For a Schwarzschild black hole we determine them by matching to the ingoing solution at the horizon. The horizon enters the amplification factor as an absorptive contact term, which reproduces the horizon-area cross section; it is absent for a non-absorbing lens of the same mass, and cannot be described by the thin-lens diffraction integral. It completes the correction quadratic in the mass, where it appears at the same order as finite-distance optical corrections, and largely cancels against them for an aligned source. Together, these results connect Newtonian dressing, diffraction and inner boundary conditions, in a systematic description of corrections to point-mass gravitational-wave lensing.

ai_review.summary: The abstract presents a scalar-wave framework for corrections to Newtonian point-mass gravitational-wave lensing. Newtonian-dressed radial kernels retain the long-range interaction while organizing additional effects by distance from the lens. The authors report that wavefront curvature modifies the direct wave as well as the scattered component, and that steeper exterior potentials require local terms fixed by the lens’s inner boundary condition. Matching to a Schwarzschild horizon supplies an absorptive contribution that reproduces the horizon-area cross section and can cancel finite-distance corrections for aligned sources. The contribution is a systematic connection between exterior lens structure and central absorption beyond the thin-lens description. Only the abstract was available here, so the matching calculation, error control and applicability to tensor gravitational waves remain unassessed.

papers.title: Detectability of Eccentric Intermediate Mass-Ratio Inspiral in the Decihertz Band
papers.abstract: The proposed decihertz gravitational-wave (GW) band $(\sim 10^{-2}-1\,\Hz)$ will observe the late inspiral of intermediate mass-ratio inspirals (IMRIs), binaries with mass ratios $10^2 \lesssim q \lesssim 10^4$ that assemble dynamically in dense stellar environments and are expected to retain measurable eccentricity. Search and parameter-estimation pipelines are predominantly built around circular templates, and we test this assumption. Using black-hole perturbation theory waveforms from \textsc{FastEMRIWaveforms} for a representative IMRI ($M=10^4\,\modot$, $q=100$, observed for its final $10\,\hr$), we compute fitting factors between eccentric signals and circular templates, maximizing over the template's total mass and mass ratio with a differential-evolution search, for the B-DECIGO, LGWA-Si, and IndIGO-D noise curves and a flat PSD. The mismatch grows with initial eccentricity $e_0$ and crosses the standard $3\%$ threshold at $e_0\simeq3\times10^{-2}$, well within the range allowed by the waveform model and expected from dynamical formation. The best-fitting circular templates also bias the total mass and mass ratio by several percent at $e_0=0.1$. Combining the mismatch with the signal-to-noise-dependent distinguishability criterion, we find that for a source at $1\,\mathrm{Gpc}$, eccentricities as small as $e_0\simeq5\times10^{-4}$ (B-DECIGO and IndIGO-D) and $5\times10^{-3}$ (LGWA-Si) are resolvable, one to two orders of magnitude below where detection efficiency degrades. The loss of match arises from the excitation of radial Teukolsky harmonics, which spread power into sidebands that circular templates cannot represent, and from the slower orbital decay of eccentric binaries at fixed initial semi-latus rectum. Robust detection and parameter estimation of IMRIs with DECIGO, LGWA, and IndIGO-D will require eccentric waveform models and template banks.

papers.title: Constraining Gamma-Ray Emission Beyond the TOV Limit: A Targeted Fermi-GBM Search for Counterparts to 39 LVK Gravitational-Wave Candidates in GWTC-5.0
papers.abstract: We present a systematic search for sub-threshold gamma-ray counterparts within a one-day time window of 161 gravitational-wave (GW) events from the GWTC-5.0 catalog, whose inferred source masses exceed the adopted Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff (TOV) limit, using the Gamma-ray Targeted Search (GTS) pipeline. The search identifies 39 candidate GW--gamma-ray pairs satisfying the adopted joint likelihood-ratio thresholds. None of these candidates exhibits a temporal offset compatible with the prompt-emission delay observed for GW170817 ($\sim 1.7$ s); the smallest temporal separation is 17 min 17.976 s, ruling out GW170817-like prompt temporal associations in our candidate sample. Several candidates nevertheless show substantial spatial consistency. In particular, the most spatially consistent pair has a joint localization overlap of 95.4%, despite a temporal separation of 13 h 19 min 8.85 s, illustrating that high spatial agreement can occur by chance in the absence of temporal consistency. Among the sub-threshold gamma-ray candidates, we further identify an anomalous event with an exceptionally large single-instrument significance of log LR = 5250.84. For comparison, the adopted $3σ$ threshold corresponds to log LR $\approx 9$. The extreme likelihood ratio of this candidate motivates further investigation of trigger sensitivity, onboard veto configurations, and the statistical interpretation of sub-threshold events. Overall, we find no physically viable multi-messenger associations between the GWTC-5.0 events and the searched gamma-ray candidates, and derive corresponding upper limits on prompt high-energy emission from GWTC-5.0 progenitors.

papers.title: Gravitational lensing and deflection angles of generalised Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole embedded in a warped braneworld background
papers.abstract: We investigate null geodesics, deflection angles, and gravitational lensing by the generalized Ellis-Bronnikov (GEB) wormhole and its embedding in a five-dimensional warped braneworld (WGEB). The GEB geometry extends the standard Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole through a steepness parameter $m\geq 2$, which controls the throat profile while partially reducing the violation of the classical energy conditions. We derive analytic expressions for the weak- and strong-deflection angles and obtain the corresponding Einstein-ring and relativistic-image relations. The standard Ellis-Bronnikov results are recovered as the special case $m=2$, while for $m>2$ the strong-deflection angle exhibits a power-law divergence instead of the familiar logarithmic behaviour. For the warped five-dimensional geometry, we show that the extra-dimensional momentum modifies the effective impact parameter, and hence the deflection angle and image positions while leaving the location of the unstable photon orbit unchanged. We further derive generalized relations between relativistic and non-relativistic Einstein-ring radii. Our analysis shows that deflection/ring data alone cannot distinguish the effect of the warped extra dimension in WGEB scenario.

papers.title: Carrollian correlators in black hole perturbation theory
papers.abstract: In this note, we clarify the relationship between the two-point Carrollian correlator and massless scattering in a black hole background. It turns out that there are two types of Carrollian correlators at the null boundaries of each asymptotically flat spacetime. The correlator from $\mathscr I^-$ to $\mathscr I^+$ should be regularized by subtracting the flat-space analog, and it is the position space version of the reflection amplitude for massless scattering. On the other hand, the correlator from $\mathscr I^-$ to the future horizon $\mathcal H^+$ is absent in flat space, and it is the position space version of the transmission amplitude. The poles of the Carrollian correlators are governed by null geodesics from $\mathscr I^-$ to either $\mathscr I^+$ or $\mathcal H^+$, and these geodesics define two classes of classical equations in Carrollian space. These equations relate the Shapiro time delay to the deflection angle and are determined purely by the boundary data. We find that, for small deflection angles, the time delay for the correlator from $\mathscr I^-$ to $\mathscr I^+/\mathcal H^+$ exhibits logarithmic/quadratic behavior. On the other hand, when the deflection angle is large, the time delay always increases linearly for both correlators. We further establish a relation between the low-frequency bulk scattering coefficients and the leading non-contact contributions at late times. The correlator from $\mathscr I^-$ to $\mathscr I^+$ features an inverse-square tail $τ^{-2}$ with an explicit angular distribution $K_2$. We have numerically confirmed this angle-dependent late-time tail.

papers.title: Geometric distinguishability of two-source gravitational-wave signals from the extrinsic geometry of the single-source waveform manifold
papers.abstract: Overlapping gravitational-wave signals can produce strong degeneracies in which a multi-source waveform is accurately represented by a single effective source. We formulate this source-confusion problem geometrically by treating the family of single-source waveforms as an embedded manifold in the noise-weighted detector Hilbert space. We introduce the distance-to-manifold statistic, defined as the minimum residual obtained by fitting a waveform with the single-source model, and show that its squared value is directly related to the maximized likelihood difference between two-source and single-source hypotheses in the noiseless limit. For two sources with nearby parameters, perturbative minimization demonstrates that the effective single-source fit absorbs all leading tangent-space deformations. The first irreducible residual lies in the normal space of the waveform manifold and is governed by its second fundamental form. We validate our approach using a six-parameter frequency-domain inspiral model with a LISA-like time-delay-interferometry response. Direct optimization reproduces the predicted quartic scaling over the numerically resolved regime, while two-dimensional confusion-zone maps reveal strongly anisotropic distinguishability boundaries. These results establish extrinsic waveform-manifold curvature as a coordinate-independent diagnostic of local multi-source confusion and provide a practical framework for identifying parameter-space directions in which overlapping gravitational-wave sources are most difficult to resolve.

papers.title: Double Blandford: Resistive GRMHD simulations of accreting black holes simultaneously launch winds and jets
papers.abstract: Magnetic fields can launch outflows through the Blandford-Znajek (BZ) or the Blandford-Payne (BP) mechanism in accreting black hole systems. Despite the dominant launching mechanism still being unclear, the BP process has been insufficiently studied in general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations due to difficulties in generating and maintaining the required large-scale magnetic field geometry. Here, we set up six resistive GRMHD simulations of thin accretion disks with BHAC. The accretion disks in two simulations become magnetically arrested, while the others stay in the standard and normal evolution (SANE) regime. All simulations form jets and winds. The jets are parabolic and collimated by the outer sub-relativistic disk wind; a power law relating the jet width $x$ to the height $z$ as $x\propto z^\mathcal{K}$ yields exponents between 0.52 and 0.64. Among the SANE simulations, the setup with spin parameter $a_* = -0.9375$ has the most efficient jet. For a highly spinning black hole with $a_*=0.9375$, the BZ jet power is $\gtrsim3$ times greater than the disk wind power. The simulated wind regions consist of a highly magnetized region, where the magnetization parameter $σ\gg1$, and a less magnetized region. A fast outflow with the potential to reach Lorentz factors up to $Γ_\infty\approx25$ propagates in the former region, but because the Lorentz force acts against the disk, it cannot remove a measurable amount of mass from the disk. In the less-magnetized region, a centrifugally driven slower wind efficiently carries away disk material.

papers.title: Post-Newtonian expansion of the energy and angular momentum flux radiated to infinity: Eccentric-equatorial orbits about a Kerr black hole
papers.abstract: We present analytical expressions for the energy and angular momentum fluxes radiated to infinity by a (nonspinning) point mass in an eccentric-equatorial orbit about a Kerr black hole. These results build upon our previous work involving point masses on eccentric orbits about a Schwarzschild black hole. We now adopt the Teukolsky formalism in first-order black hole perturbation theory to extend our methods to Kerr. We obtain the expressions using the method of Mano, Suzuki, and Takasugi, which provides infinite-series analytical solutions to the Teukolsky equation that we generate using Mathematica. The expressions presented are obtained as a double expansion in the post-Newtonian (PN) compactness parameter $1/p$, where $p$ is the dimensionless semi-latus rectum, and in the eccentricity $e$, up to 10PN and $e^{20}$, extending beyond prior 6PN and $e^{16}$ results available for generic orbits. We characterize how the PN flux coefficients depend on the black hole spin $a$ and $e$, and find a set of spin-dependent components that can be resummed as closed-form expressions in $e$. The analytical expressions are then validated with numerical comparisons against high-precision sample results from an independent Teukolsky code and with a broader set of numerically interpolated values derived from a flux data set produced with the same code. For $a=0.9M$, the numerically evaluated 10PN fluxes match current interpolated flux grids ($\sim10^{-7}$) for $p\gtrsim20$ to $75$ as $e$ ranges from $0.1$ to $0.7$, where they could replace Teukolsky-code results.

papers.title: Imprints of quantum space in the ringdown phase of Kerr black holes
papers.abstract: We investigate quantum-space corrections to the gravitational quasinormal modes (QNMs) of Kerr black holes within the framework of noncommutative geometry. The analysis employs a pseudo-semi-Killing Drinfeld twist, which preserves the classical Kerr geometry as an exact background solution while introducing nontrivial quantum corrections to linearized gravitational perturbations. Working to first order in the black hole spin and the quantum deformation parameter, including their mixed contribution, we derive a Schrödinger-like master equation for axial gravitational perturbations with a frequency- and spin-dependent effective potential. We compute the fundamental QNM frequencies using the WKB approximation and Leaver's continued-fraction method.Our results reveal corrections to the QNM oscillation frequencies and damping rates arising from rotation, pure quantum effects, and their interplay.To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic analysis of gravitational metric perturbations in a noncommutative Kerr black hole spacetime using a Drinfeld twist, extending prior work beyond the Schwarzschild case. Our findings demonstrate that quantum deformation effects alter both the oscillation frequencies and damping rates of quasinormal modes, with spin-quantum coupling introducing additional spin-dependent corrections to the Kerr QNM spectrum. Using a Kerr-anchored phenomenological prescription, we estimate the fractional frequency and damping-time shifts for selected merger remnants from the GWTC-3 and GWTC-5.0 catalogs. These estimates illustrate the potential signatures of quantum corrections in gravitational-wave ringdown.

papers.title: How Bright in Gravitational Waves are Millisecond Pulsars for the Galactic Center GeV Gamma-Ray Excess? A Systematic Study and Implications for Dark Matter
papers.abstract: The existence of dark matter (DM) is supported by various macroscopic observations, but its microscopic nature remains elusive. The Galactic Center GeV gamma-ray excess (GCE) has been a leading candidate signal for particle DM annihilation. However, an unresolved population of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) in the bulge provides the alternative explanation for the excess. Identifying these MSPs in electromagnetic bands is difficult due to source confusion, pulse broadening, and extinction. Gravitational waves (GWs) provide a complementary probe: a steadily rotating, non-axisymmetric MSP emits a nearly monochromatic GW signal in the sensitive band of ground-based detectors, with amplitude set by its ellipticity. In this work, we systematically investigate the GW emission from the MSP population proposed to explain the GCE and its detectability with current and future detectors. We consider three major scenarios for the origin of ellipticity and model the population properties of these MSPs. We also consider both isolated MSPs and MSPs in binary systems, as well as Doppler effects in the detection. We find that while the signal is below the reach of current interferometers, next-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope (ET) and Cosmic Explorer (CE) may detect a fraction of those MSPs, offering a novel test of the MSP interpretation of the GCE. Future directed searches toward the Galactic Center may either uncover this long-sought MSP population or place stringent constraints on bulge MSP properties. Continued improvements in detector sensitivity will provide increasingly stringent tests of the MSP interpretation, with growing power to distinguish between the astrophysical and DM interpretations of the GCE.

papers.title: Ionization of gravitational atoms by a companion-sourced Yukawa potential
papers.abstract: Superradiant instabilities around rotating black holes can produce clouds of ultralight bosons bound by the black hole's gravitational field. A binary companion can ionize these clouds by driving transitions into continuum states in the black hole's 1/r gravitational potential, extracting energy and angular momentum from the orbit. We investigate how a companion-sourced Yukawa interaction modifies this process. At weak coupling, the interference term between the gravitational and Yukawa transition amplitudes provides the leading correction to the ionization power. For the orbital frequencies here, an attractive interaction enhances continuum ionization and accelerates the inspiral, whereas a repulsive interaction has the opposite effect. At larger coupling, the pure Yukawa contribution to the ionization power becomes increasingly important and can compete with the gravitational contribution, particularly for lighter mediators. Comparing continuum ionization with off-resonant bound-state mixing, we find that continuum ionization can halt superradiant growth at a substantially smaller Yukawa coupling. At their respective critical couplings, the Yukawa interaction provides the dominant contribution to cloud depletion in both channels. Finally, we calculate the phase correction to gravitational waves due to continuum ionization and characterize how the chirp-rate response varies with frequency near the thresholds at which successive orbital harmonics open continuum-ionization channels.

papers.title: Gravitational waves in hierarchical triples with lensing and relativistic orbits
papers.abstract: Binary black holes (BBH) may be formed near galactic nuclei. If such BBH systems exist, modulations to the gravitational waveform through time delays, lensing, and angular momentum precession could allow the presence of the third body to be measured in this system. In this letter, we advance the modeling for hierarchical triples by carefully including new relativistic lensing, aberration, and polarization terms. We show that the gravitational waves from this system can be computed exactly in the geometric optics limit by ray tracing the null geodesics and parallel transporting their polarization without a weak-field expansion. Our construction evolves the inner binary as if it were a post-Newtonian signal, and computes the environmental modulations efficiently with elliptic integrals. We find that this method improves the accuracy of such a triple waveform significantly compared to previous post-Newtonian approximations, and allows numerically efficient computation of the modulations. This lays the groundwork for future hierarchical triple waveform codebases, which can be used in LISA parameter estimation and detectability.

papers.title: Equivalence of mapping gravitational wave background anisotropy across bases at equal information content
papers.abstract: Mapping anisotropies in the gravitational-wave background (GWB) requires choosing a basis to represent the sky intensity, such as pixel and spherical harmonic bases. Each introduces a truncation---e.g., a number of pixels or a maximum multipole l_max---often set by a naive counting argument that relate the number of measurable modes to the number of independent cross-correlations, N_pair, in a pulsar timing array (PTA). However, such truncations can lead to reconstruction artifacts, as they do not reflect the true information content of the PTA response. Increasing the value of truncation parameters spans the observable space better but reveals poorly constrained modes, making the inverse problem ill conditioned and requiring regularization. A natural approach is to restrict the reconstruction to a well-measured subspace via principal maps, defined by the dominant eigenmodes of the detector response (or Fisher) matrix. However, these maps are not a fundamental parametrization of the sky but, rather, are derived from an underlying representation---such as a pixelization or a spherical harmonic expansion. While their explicit form depends on basis choice, they can span the \textit{same subspace} when the underlying representation is sufficiently complete. Here, we show that reconstructed anisotropy maps via different bases are equivalent, provided they retain the same information content, i.e., span the same principal subspace. As illustrative cases, we consider a toy model for PTA configuration and several GWB anisotropy shapes: point source, an extended source with deterministic anisotropy, and a statistical isotropic background, along with its summary statistic---the angular power spectrum. Although the reconstructions are equivalent, their computational costs can differ. We conclude with brief comments on the construction of principal maps for ground-based interferometers.

papers.title: How graviton mass shapes angular correlations in a relic gravitational-wave background
papers.abstract: A nonzero graviton mass makes waves emitted at the same epoch travel different distances at different momenta. A finite band therefore samples a shell that is both closer to the observer and thicker. We derive the distribution of source radii and use it to calculate the band angular-power ratio $C_\ell^{BB}(m_{\rm g})/C_\ell^{BB}(0)$ for a relic stochastic gravitational-wave background. For a common source field with a scale-invariant spatial spectrum, a thin shell has the same angular power at every radius. Radial averaging cannot exceed this power, so any suppression relative to the massless single-epoch spectrum is due to shell broadening. We also ask whether source mixing can mimic massive propagation across two frequency bands. For two independent emission episodes whose mixing fractions are fixed across multipoles, massless propagation requires the low-band auto-power and the cross-power, each normalized by the high-band auto-power, to lie on a straight line when plotted against one another. This holds for arbitrary angular spectra of the two sources. A massive benchmark near the low-band propagation threshold violates this relation. A joint massless fit with power-law sources nevertheless gives an rms logarithmic residual of $0.013$ over $2\leq\ell\leq10$.

papers.title: Quasinormal Modes and Excitation Factors of a Parity-Symmetric Beyond-Horndeski Black Hole
papers.abstract: We study scalar, electromagnetic, and Dirac perturbations of an asymptotically flat black hole in parity-symmetric beyond-Horndeski gravity. The quasinormal spectrum is computed with very-high-order WKB expansions and Padé resummation, with Cesàro means used to diagnose internal convergence. The dominant modes are independently tested by time-domain evolution with Prony extraction and by Chebyshev pseudospectral collocation; the latter also provides systematic frequency scans in both the metric-scale and physical ADM-mass normalizations. Excitation factors are obtained separately from Green-function residues by complex-contour integration. In the fixed metric-scale normalization, approaching Schwarzschild generally increases both the oscillation frequency and damping rate, whereas stronger deformation shifts the modes toward lower frequencies and weaker damping. In ADM-mass units, the mildly deformed solutions remain close to Schwarzschild, while the most deformed sector becomes enhanced and nonmonotonic because the asymptotic mass itself varies strongly. The independent methods agree very well, however the sixth-order WKB approximation used in [G. Antoniou, T. D. Pappas, P. Kanti, Phys. Rev. D 112, 084013 (2025)] is insufficient in certain regions of the parameter space: the fundamental-mode discrepancy reaches nine percent in the damping rate and the first-overtone discrepancy can be of order unity. The Schwarzschild excitation factors are recovered. In the strongly deformed regime, their magnitudes can differ from the Schwarzschild values by more than two orders of magnitude in the asymptotic tortoise-coordinate convention. We show that this large effect is predominantly due to the deformation-dependent displacement of the potential barrier in the tortoise coordinate: when its maximum is used as the origin, the excitation factors exhibit much more modest deviations.

papers.title: Exactly solvable Brill waves: explicit gravitational-wave initial data with trapped surfaces
papers.abstract: Vacuum initial data for pure gravitational waves on $\mathbb{R}^3$ (Brill waves) have so far been obtained only numerically. Here a one-parameter family is solved exactly: in toroidal coordinates the constraint separates, and a suitable seed function makes every mode equation hypergeometric. The data are real analytic and asymptotically flat and exist precisely for $k<k_c=0.8048\ldots$; their mass is an explicit series with a pole at $k_c$. Near $k_c$ the data provably contain trapped surfaces and an apparent horizon. A scaling symmetry yields further solvable families, one of them elementary.

papers.title: Assessing the imprint of eccentricity in GW signatures using two independent waveform models
papers.abstract: The gravitational-wave signal from merging compact binaries encodes information about their orbital and intrinsic properties. Over the last few years, state-of-the-art waveform models have begun to incorporate the effects of orbital eccentricity into their estimated signal. Over a similar period, many groups have applied these waveforms to characterize whether the imprint of eccentricity is present and, if so, measure this time-evolving property (at a suitably-defined reference point). In this work, we present a comprehensive analysis of 162 confident sources identified in the O3 and O4a observing runs of the International Gravitational Wave Network (LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA). Using the RIFT parameter inference engine, we employ two independently implemented waveform models (SEOBNRv5EHM and TEOBResumS-Dali) which account for orbital eccentricity and the effects of aligned compact object spins. Using these two waveforms, we find consistent conclusions that disfavor the eccentric hypothesis. Unlike previous work, among binary black hole candidates, we find potential evidence for eccentricity in three events: GW200129, GW231001, and GW231123. For the latter two events, the evidence for eccentricity is ambiguous, with different degrees of support from different waveforms. Consistent with previous work, we find conclusions obtained about GW200129 can be sensitive to analysis settings, as expected, given the nonstationary noise present.

papers.title: Long-Term Evolution of Hills-Captured Stars with TDE Disk Collisions: Links to Repeating Nuclear Transients
papers.abstract: Quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs) and repeating partial tidal disruption event (rpTDE) candidates are widely interpreted as being powered by a star on an hours-to-years orbit around a massive black hole (MBH). Every such orbiter model presupposes a star delivered onto an extraordinarily compact orbit without being destroyed, but it is unclear whether this is achievable. We follow the coupled orbital and stellar evolution of stars captured by the Hills mechanism, combining gas drag and per-collision mass loss from recurrent TDE disks with gravitational-wave (GW) orbital decay and stochastic two-body relaxation in a Monte Carlo model. Conventionally, the EMRI-formation criterion is based on comparing the timescales of GW decay and orbital angular momentum relaxation. We find that this criterion severely overestimates the EMRI rate: for relaxation timescales shorter than a Hubble time, most Hills-captured stars are tidally disrupted before GW emission can circularize the stellar orbit. Instead, TDE-disk drag plays a crucial role in the orbital evolution and can boost the fraction of stars reaching QPE orbits by an order of magnitude or more, assuming that the disk aspect ratio is relatively large $H/r \sim 0.1$. We also find that collisional ablation imposes a minimum orbital period that rises with MBH mass and precludes sub-day orbits for $M_{\rm BH} \gtrsim 10^6\,M_\odot$, unless GWs alone can drive orbital decay faster than orbital relaxation. This can explain the observed preference of short-period QPEs for low-mass MBHs. Most known rpTDEs lie below the Hills-capture period minimum and thus require additional orbital decay, which TDE-disk drag can plausibly supply. These results support the viability of the orbiter model; our predictions of the MBH mass and orbital period distributions can be used to further test this model.

papers.title: Disrupted stars and captured compact objects: Combining observations from multiple messengers to infer the population of massive black holes
papers.abstract: Massive black holes (MBHs) are found in galactic centres, but their formation and evolution remain elusive. Tidal disruption events (TDEs) and extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) both arise from stellar dynamics in the nuclear star clusters around MBHs, and are observed with electromagnetic surveys and gravitational waves, respectively. To overcome the scarcity of coincident detections, we formulate how to combine gravitational-wave detections from LISA-EMRIs with observations from ZTF-TDEs to measure properties of the MBH population. Building on two-dimensional Fokker-Planck simulations of EMRIs and TDEs, we model how their populations are affected by the MBH-host scaling relation, the nucleation fraction and the MBH occupation fraction, and analyse the resulting catalogues using joint hierarchical inference accounting for their individual selection biases. With current ZTF-TDE detections, we can already identify combinations of MBH formation favoured by and consistent with the observed TDE population, and derive corresponding predictions for the EMRI population detectable by LISA. Across a range of astrophysical assumptions, the ratio of detectable TDEs to EMRIs is high: ZTF detecting 2.7-84.3 times as many TDEs as LISA detects EMRIs. TDEs, through their numbers, set the shared mass and redshift distributions: LSST constrains the characteristic MBH mass to a 90% credible width of 0.31 dex and the power-law index of the redshift evolution to a precision of 0.11. EMRIs make up ~3.4% of the joint catalogue, yet carry more information than the whole ZTF sample and are the only probe of MBH spin and orbital eccentricity. TDEs will constrain the abundance of low-mass MBHs before LISA flies, while EMRIs will measure properties that electromagnetic surveys cannot. EMRI and TDE observations offer complementary insights into MBH growth and evolution that neither can provide alone.

papers.title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
papers.abstract: Scalar-induced second-order tensor perturbations comprise both a forced response and freely propagating gravitational waves, the radiative signal sought in gravitational-wave observations. We define this free radiation as the out-state, extracted from the light-cone residue of the kernel for each scalar pair via a classical LSZ-type reduction formula. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: tensor redefinitions with power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leave the out-state invariant. For any constant equation of state $0<w<1$, the out-state is consequently universal across all intrinsic gauges, where slicing and spatial coordinates are fixed by local matter and geometry without an external clock. In this regime, the late-time Newtonian-gauge kernel yields the out-state, rigorously justifying the standard practice of computing the scalar-induced gravitational-wave energy spectrum from this kernel.

papers.title: A Relativistic Newton's Third Law for Binaries in Environments
papers.abstract: We derive the relativistic form of Newton's Third Law governing the interaction between intermediate- and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals and surrounding relativistic matter fields. Working within a two-parameter expansion, we rewrite the evolution of the secondary's orbital elements in a form resembling the integrated forces acting on the environment, avoiding the need to calculate any gravitational perturbations sourced by the dynamical matter content. Using the retarded and advanced Green's functions, we obtain both instantaneous and orbit-averaged laws relating the rate of change of the secondary's orbital energy and angular momentum to that of the matter and the gravitational-wave fluxes at that order. Our results clarify and correct the mixture of ad hoc balance prescriptions currently employed in the literature, providing first-principles forcing functions for the secondary's orbital elements in two ready-to-use forms: a leading-order formulation suitable for fast evaluation with complex relativistic matter simulations, and a first-post-adiabatic formulation of the energy and angular-momentum evolution in environments that are stationary and axisymmetric at leading order.

papers.title: Type-II quasinormal modes of dilaton--Euler--Heisenberg AdS black holes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate Type-II quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a magnetically charged dilaton--Euler--Heisenberg black hole in anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime. The Type-II includes coupled gravitational, dilaton and electromagnetic perturbations. Its coupled equations are derived for $\ell=0,1,2$ modes and the QNM frequencies are calculated by employing direct integration and Chebyshev pseudospectral methods, giving consistent results. For nondegenerate dipole ($\ell=1$) mode at fixed curvature, the nonlinear correction starts at order $Q^2$ for electromagnetic-led branch and at order $Q^4$ for scalar-led branch. In this case, stronger AdS curvature enhances reduction of the electromagnetic-led real frequency for positive coupling, while gravitational-led quadrupole real frequency changes weakly with charge. As the curvature weakens, the dipole frequencies approach the AdS normal-mode scale and their damping decreases. We find that all modes computed have negative imaginary parts for nonextremal black holes, implying this black hole is stable against Type-II perturbations. Furthermore, we explore the connection between thermodynamic phase transition and QNMs for $\ell=0$ dilaton. For a subcritical isobaric process, the QNM real frequency of $\ell=0$ dilaton decreases with increasing temperature of small black holes, while it increases with increasing temperature of large black holes. At coexistence, the damping rate for large black holes is about 4.28 times that for small black holes.

papers.title: Eccentric and unbound compact binaries in the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA catalog: parameter estimation and waveform systematics with SEOBNRv6EHM
papers.abstract: Orbital eccentricity encodes key information about compact-binary formation channels and astrophysical environments, making it a critical target for gravitational-wave (GW) inference. We present parameter-estimation (PE) analyses of GWs from eccentric compact binaries with the SEOBNRv6EHM waveform model. Using long, highly eccentric numerical-relativity waveforms as synthetic signals, we compare parameter recovery across state-of-the-art eccentric models. We find that SEOBNRv5EHM and TEOBResumS-Dalí can yield biased estimates of eccentricity, masses, and spins in the most challenging configurations, while SEOBNRv6EHM significantly reduces these biases. Applying SEOBNRv6EHM to 26 GW events from the O1--O4 LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA observing runs---including binary black hole, neutron-star--black-hole, and binary neutron-star mergers---we identify five events with mild support for eccentricity over the quasi-circular precessing-spin hypothesis, with Bayes factors $\log_{10} \mathcal{B}^{\text{EAS}}_{\text{QCP}} > 0.5$. Since SEOBNRv6EHM is applicable to generic planar binaries, we reanalyze five high-mass events allowing for unbound initial conditions. For three of them---including GW190521, previously claimed to originate from a dynamical capture---a direct-capture configuration is comparable to, or marginally favored over, both the eccentric aligned-spin and quasi-circular precessing-spin hypotheses ($\log_{10}\mathcal{B}^{\rm unbound}_{\rm QCP} \approx 0.2$--$0.6$ for GW190521). The recovered configurations are, however, astrophysically unrealistic and cannot be confidently discriminated from highly eccentric bound orbits, so these results do not, by themselves, support an unbound origin for these events. SEOBNRv6EHM is approximately three times faster in PE analyses than SEOBNRv5EHM, while improving waveform accuracy, enabling efficient, large-scale GW inference with eccentric waveforms.

papers.title: Lost in the Signal Model: Confusion Between Deterministic and Stochastic Gravitational Wave Signals in Pulsar Timing Array Data
papers.abstract: With growing evidence for the presence of a gravitational wave background (GWB) in pulsar timing array (PTA) data, it is imperative to understand how this signal will act as a foreground for other GW signals, particularly those from individual supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs), which are predicted to be detected in the next decade. For PTAs, since these two types of signals are long-timescale persistent signals, a signal from an SMBHB system may already be present in the latest PTA datasets. In this work, we analyze how the presence of this signal could affect our detection statistics for the GWB, and how the presence of the GWB can affect our search for the SMBHB system. We find that individual SMBHB signals can significantly skew the recovery of the GWB amplitude and spectral index. However, when the SMBHB signals are recovered consistently, we are again able to recover the GWB power-law parameters, highlighting the importance of joint searches in future PTA searches for GWs. We also explore the rate of improvement of parameter estimation uncertainty, giving insight to the types of signals most likely to be identified well enough to enable multimessenger analyses.

papers.title: Prospects for multi-messenger discovery of the gravitational-wave background anisotropies via cross-correlation with galaxies
papers.abstract: We present new empirically grounded forecasts for the observability of stochastic gravitational-wave background anisotropies assuming a population of stellar-mass compact binary coalescences as its source. We quantified the discovery potential using simulations based on the Euclid Flagship Galaxy Catalogue and LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observational constraints in combination with detailed theoretical modelling. We considered the multi-messenger cross-correlation with galaxies as well as the gravitational wave-only cross-correlation across observation-time bins. We found that signal-to-noise ratio greater than five is achievable via cross-correlation of a galaxy catalogue that is complete up to limiting magnitude $i < 24.7$ and has redshift uncertainties $σ_z = 0.003 (1+z)$ with a gravitational-wave sky map corresponding to 2 years of observation by a third-generation detector network comprising three interferometers. Network configurations with LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA plus up to two third-generation detectors would be limited to moderate signal-to-noise levels, between three and five, except if merger rates are near the upper bound set by observational constraints, in which case the threshold of five would be reached after 4 years. Detectability without the multi-messenger tracer has proven significantly more challenging, with signal-to-noise ratio remaining below three after 10 years. In light of the plans being carried out in the community for ongoing and upcoming galaxy surveys, this work bodes well for the multi-messenger discovery and exploration of the stochastic gravitational-wave background in the era of next-generation observatories such as the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer.

papers.title: Probing the dynamical inverse seesaw mechanism with low-frequency gravitational waves
papers.abstract: We study the possibility of probing the dynamical inverse seesaw mechanism for the origin of light neutrino masses via the detection of stochastic gravitational waves (GW) in the low-frequency regime currently being probed by pulsar timing arrays. As the lepton number-violating term in inverse seesaw typically remains in the sub-MeV ballpark, its dynamical origin naturally brings the possibility of a low-scale first-order phase transition, which can be probed at low-frequency GW experiments. We also find interesting complementarity with heavy neutral lepton searches, as GW experiments remain sensitive to parameter space with small active-sterile mixing, which is out of reach for most particle physics experiments.

papers.title: Perturbations in the parametrized wormhole spacetime and their related quasinormal modes
papers.abstract: We study electromagnetic perturbations and the associated quasinormal modes (QNMs) of parametrized static, spherically symmetric wormhole spacetimes, focusing on Damour-Solodukhin and braneworld geometries as well as their galactic extensions. Using the Bronnikov-Konoplya-Pappas (BKP) parametrization, we express the metric functions in terms of a compactified radial coordinate and characterize the spacetime through far-field and near-throat parameters. The far-field coefficients govern the asymptotic structure and post-Newtonian behaviour, while the near-throat continued-fraction expansion captures the strong-field geometry near the throat. We first apply the parametrization to isolated wormholes and identify its range of validity, showing that the non-analytic metric functions can limit the applicability of the BKP scheme. Moreover we have shown that such issues can indeed hamper the primary ringdown waveform. We then extend the framework to a galactic Damour-Solodukhin wormhole embedded in a Hernquist dark matter halo. Imposing observational bounds from the shadow of Sgr A$^*$, we constrain the galactic compactness and deformation parameters and obtain an observationally viable parametrized metric. Within the allowed parameter space, we compute the fundamental QNM frequencies using the transfer matrix method and analyze the corresponding time-domain ringdown signals. We find that the damping rate is more sensitive to galactic compactness, whereas the oscillation frequency remains comparatively stable. Although the spectral shifts are small within the shadow-allowed region, the framework provides a systematic link between geometric parametrization, shadow constraints, and dynamical response. Our results establish an observationally consistent parametrized description of wormhole perturbations for strong-field tests of horizonless compact objects.

papers.title: Thermal Resummation Effects on Electroweak Phase Transitions and Gravitational Waves in Conformal and Non-Conformal 2HDMs
papers.abstract: We quantify how thermal resummation affects electroweak phase transitions and gravitational-wave predictions in classically conformal and non-conformal two-Higgs-doublet models. We compare multi-field partial dressing (PD), which retains the full thermal functions and determines scalar masses and mixing from gap equations, with the Parwani and Arnold-Espinosa (AE) prescriptions at identical zero-temperature inputs. Completed first-order transitions dominate the conformal scan under all three prescriptions. PD typically gives the strongest and most supercooled transitions, reaching $T_p/T_c \simeq 0.5$ versus $T_p/T_c \gtrsim 0.8$ for Parwani and AE. At every conformal point where all three predict completion, PD gives the largest gravitational-wave peak amplitude, followed by Parwani and AE. The non-conformal model has no universal ordering, and the prescription changes the type of thermal history across extended regions of parameter space. For representative benchmarks, PD and AE differ by up to about nine orders of magnitude in peak amplitude and a factor of about fifty in peak frequency. In multi-field PD, the dressed tadpole is not a gradient, so the reconstructed potential depends on the integration path. In benchmark tests, changing the path shifts the transition temperatures by at most about 7% and the peak amplitude by up to a factor of about three. This intrinsic ambiguity is smaller than the largest differences between prescriptions. Thermal resummation is a major source of uncertainty in these phase-transition and gravitational-wave predictions.

papers.title: Peanut/X-shaped bulges: Returning to the vertical resonance and separatrix
papers.abstract: We investigate the vertical structure and evolution of an $N$-body galactic bar by analyzing pure resonant orbits that form the skeleton of boxy/peanut/X-shaped (BP/X) bulges in Cartesian and action-angle spaces ($θ_\text{res} = θ_z - θ_R, \, J_z$). We show that the main backbone of this skeleton is made up of separatrix orbits associated with unstable figure-of-eight resonant orbits. For the first time, we examine the long-term behavior of the separatrix, showing how it sinks to the bottom of phase space and shrinks. As a result, ``fresh'' orbits involved in a flat bar are captured into vertical resonance, passing through it near the separatrix and creating orbital crowding. This crowding traces the thickest part of the BP/X bulge and outlines the ends of its X-structure rays. The rise of orbits leads to changes in the potential and geometry of phase space in these regions. Over time, when the rise ceases, evolution slows and stops.

papers.title: The gravitational wave candidate S251112cm: near-complete optical coverage with ATLAS, Pan-STARRS and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory
papers.abstract: On 2025 November 12, the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) network detected S251112cm, a compact binary merger candidate with a false alarm rate of one per four years at a luminosity distance of $93 \pm 27$ Mpc. The probability that the lighter component's mass lies below 1 $M_\odot$ is >99%, while the probability that either component lies at 1-3 $M_\odot$ is only 8%, leaving the nature of the progenitor system unclear. We present Pan-STARRS and ATLAS optical follow-up of the 90% localisation region, and quantify Vera C. Rubin Observatory target-of-opportunity observations. In the North, Pan-STARRS imaged 1084 deg$^2$ (65%) within 7 days to a median depth of 21.9 mag and ATLAS 1545 deg$^2$ (87%) within 14 days to 19.3 mag across both hemispheres; in the South, Rubin covered 849 deg$^2$ (36%) 2-10 days post-merger to median depths of 24.5 ($g$) and 23.5 ($i$) mag. They reported 173, 93 and 67 candidates respectively (269 unique), which we assess against AT 2017gfo-like kilonova and SN 1998bw-like broad-lined Type Ic supernova models using prior activity, host luminosity distance, photometric evolution and absolute magnitude. Eight survive, mainly for lack of distance information. Six of these lie in hosts fainter than any in a volume-limited comparison sample, suggesting they are background sources. AT 2025aimy declines too slowly for the AT 2017gfo-like model, and a VLT host spectrum places AT 2025alqe outside the LVK volume, leaving no convincing counterpart candidates. Pan-STARRS and Rubin together exclude both models in $\sim$80% of the 90% localisation volume: the deepest wide-area constraint on a subsolar-mass merger to date and, to our knowledge, the most complete optical coverage of a significant subsolar-mass candidate.

papers.title: GRMHD accretion beyond the black hole paradigm: Light from within the shadow
papers.abstract: We present the first three-dimensional general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulation of sustained accretion onto a horizonless singularity in which matter reaches the central object rather than being accumulated outside of it or expelled in outflows. We consider a Joshi-Malafarina-Narayan (JMN-1) spacetime, a well-motivated black hole mimicker that arises from gravitational collapse with anisotropic pressure in general relativity, and adopt a compactness parameter for which the central singularity is null. We find that the system evolves into a sustained magnetically arrested disk state. For parameters appropriate to the low-luminosity active galactic nucleus M87*, we obtain an accretion rate of $\sim(3.0 \pm 0.5)\times 10^{-6} \dot{M}_{\rm Edd}$, in full agreement with estimates based on black hole models and, in particular, comparable to that of our reference Schwarzschild black hole simulation. Synthetic ray-traced images at $230\,{\rm GHz}$, computed using polarized general relativistic radiative transfer, are broadly consistent with the Event Horizon Telescope observations of M87*. We identify a key observational discriminant between a black hole and JMN-1: the presence of detectable brightness inside of the ``observable" shadow of JMN-1. This emission originates very close to the central singularity, in a region that would be hidden behind the event horizon in a black hole spacetime. Although this signature is beyond the reach of current observations, it falls within the projected imaging dynamic range of next-generation radio interferometric instruments, offering a robust test of the black hole paradigm.
authors: Elisabete M. de Gouveia Dal Pino

papers.title: Two-dimensional Pulsar Distance Inference from Nanohertz Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: Pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) are limited in localizing nanohertz continuous gravitational waves (CGWs) by uncertainties in pulsar distances. We introduce a method to infer pulsar distances in two dimensions, using phase information from the pulsar terms of multiple CGW sources. Our approach can enhance distance precision relative to existing one-dimensional distance-inference methods. Using idealized SKA-motivated PTA simulations with prospective pulsar-distance priors, we combine information from five high-SNR CGW sources with known sky positions and luminosity distances. For example, our method achieves subparsec precision for a simulated pulsar at $0.8\,\mathrm{kpc}$ in $40\%$ of realizations, compared with none for the existing one-dimensional method. Such improvements in pulsar-distance precision could facilitate CGW host-galaxy identification and multimessenger observational prospects.

papers.title: Monopoles, Strings, Walls and Gravitational waves
papers.abstract: The gauge symmetry breaking $SU(2) \to U(1) \to Z_2 \to 1$ successively produces monopoles, strings and domain walls bounded by strings (WBS), with the elementary monopole carrying a $U(1)$ magnetic flux twice as large as the elementary string. The elementary strings and subsequently WBS emit gravitational waves, and during their decay, the WBS yield a network of composite strings that carry the same $U(1)$ flux as the monopoles. Depending on the cosmological evolution, we provide the gravitational wave spectra generated by the elementary strings and WBS, in combination with the composite strings which are either effectively stable, quasistable, or metastable. These three scenarios are also realized in the symmetry breaking chain $SU(3) \to SO(3) \to Z_2 \to 1$. Both $SU(2)$ and $SU(3)$ have appeared in the literature as flavor gauge symmetries.

papers.title: Tidal heating effects in binary black hole mergers
papers.abstract: A black hole binary approaching merger undergoes changes in its inspiral rate as energy and angular momentum are lost from the orbits into the horizons. This effect strengthens as the black holes come closer. We use numerical relativity data to model this so-called tidal heating in the strong gravity regime. We present a frequency-domain approximant for nonspinning black hole binaries that accounts for tidal heating effects up to the merger frequency. The approximant includes horizon parameters that characterize the nature of the compact objects. By applying this model to a binary black hole baseline that incorporates tidal heating, one can construct a more accurate point-particle waveform, one that is devoid of finite-size effects of the component objects. We also discuss its ramifications in modeling binary neutron star systems.

papers.title: Resonant Cavity Searches for Millicharged Dark Matter
papers.abstract: A plethora of resonant cavity experiments have been designed to search for ultralight dark matter (DM) candidates, such as axion or dark-photon DM.
